A_target.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an [[Definition:Inductive Set|inductive set]], as given by the [[Axiom of Infinity]], and $\omega$ the intersection of all inductive subsets of $\Omega$.
Then $\omega$ is the smallest inductive set, $\omega = \set \O \cup \set {x \cup \set x: x \in \omega}$, and every inductive subset of $\omega$ equals $\omega$.

B_source.statement:
Let $\Phi$ be an [[Definition:Increasing Mapping|increasing mapping]] on $\powerset \Omega$.
Then $\displaystyle \map {\operatorname {lfp} } \Phi = \bigcap \set {X: \map \Phi X \subseteq X}$ is the [[Definition:Least Fixed Point|least fixed point]] of $\Phi$.
This is the [[Knaster-Tarski Theorem]].

substitutions.the operator Phi: X -> {empty set} together with the successors of members of X

object_map.reformulation: Encode inductiveness as being a prefixed point of the zero-and-successor operator.

validity_conditions: Phi maps subsets of Omega into Omega because Omega is inductive.
The intersection does not depend on the choice of Omega, since any inductive set meets Omega in an inductive set.
proof_plan: Let $\map \Phi X = \set \O \cup \set {x \cup \set x: x \in X}$ for $X \subseteq \Omega$; as $\Omega$ is inductive, $\map \Phi X \subseteq \Omega$, and $\Phi$ is increasing.
By the source result, $\omega$ is the least fixed point of $\Phi$, so $\map \Phi \omega = \omega$: each element of $\omega$ is $\O$ or a successor.
